summary: Selection and ranking guidance for deciding which active transits matter most before interpretation is looked up.
body: Use this as the transit significance layer. It ranks active contacts before meaning is rendered. It does not interpret the transit itself; once a transit is selected, the app should look up the appropriate transit-to-natal, transit-house, or event-example content.
definition: Transit significance is the weighting process that prioritizes active transits by transiting body, aspect, natal target, tightness, applying or separating motion, angularity, natal emphasis, and larger timing context.
appUsage: Compute candidate active transits first, then rank them by significance rather than tightest orb alone.
Use the numeric model as a tunable starting point, not a fixed doctrine.
Select top transits per product lane, such as Business, Creative, and Self.
Always interpret the selected transit through natal promise, house context, and broader timing testimony.
Do not let a high score become a deterministic event prediction.
note: Imported from approved project transit-significance material. Source file was not copied into the repository.

scoringModel.note: Weights are a proposed starting model. Relative priority is meaningful; exact numbers should be calibrated against real app output.
scoringModel.formula: score = bodyWeight * aspectWeight * targetWeight * tightnessFactor * applyingFactor
scoringModel.natalEmphasisBonus: Multiply the target weight by about 1.3 when the natal point is heavily aspected, angular, close to an angle, chart-ruling, or otherwise repeated in the chart.

applyingFactor.note: Applying aspects are building and should rank above separating aspects with otherwise similar testimony.

priorityFlags.slowPlanetOnAngle: When Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, or Pluto conjoins Ascendant, IC, Descendant, or MC, flag the window around exact as a major period even if ordinary scoring would rank another transit higher.
priorityFlags.outerPlanetSignOrHouseChange: Flag when Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, or Pluto changes sign or enters a new natal house. Treat this as a shift of background theme, not one isolated event.

eclipseRules.countsWhen: Prioritize eclipses within about 4 degrees of conjunction, square, or opposition to the Sun, Moon, an angle, or a heavily emphasized natal planet.

nodeFlavor.northNode: Opening, appetite, increase, invitation, or directional pull.
nodeFlavor.southNode: Release, reduction, completion, letting go, or draining away.

eclipseRules.lunarVsSolar: Lunar eclipses often land emotionally and are felt most strongly in the days before exact. Solar eclipses are more likely to describe external or event-like shifts when the chart repeats the theme.

prohibitions: Do not interpret from the score alone.
Do not turn a high-ranking transit into a guaranteed event.
Do not let outer-planet background contacts dominate daily check-ins unless they are tight, angular, repeated, or hitting personal planets.
Do not rank eclipses as important unless they contact a meaningful natal point or house topic.
weighting: Angles, Sun, Moon, chart ruler, sect light, and activated time lords outrank background contacts.
Applying aspects rank higher than separating aspects when other factors are similar.
Tightness matters, but exactness alone is not enough if the natal target is low-relevance.
Slow planets on angles can describe major periods and deserve priority flags.
Daily lanes should select the strongest few transits rather than overloading the user with every active contact.
